title: Shadows of Thornwick
summary: A fishing village is vanishing one soul at a time. Unravel the ancient bargain that built Thornwick — before the tide comes in for good.
world: Thornwick is a fishing village of two hundred souls on the Estuary Coast, where the River Wend meets the Greywater Sea. Its cliffs are jagged basalt, its tides unpredictable, and its fog permanent from autumn through spring. The village has survived centuries by smoking fish, selling barge passage upriver, and keeping its own counsel — no one from Thornwick gossips outside of Thornwick. Three months ago the Harbormaster, a stout woman named Brek, disappeared without a trace. Two weeks after that, fishers began reporting lights beneath the water at night: cold blue-green lights that moved with purpose, following the boats. Then the disappearances resumed — one or two a fortnight, always at night, always people who'd been alone near the water. The surviving villagers are frightened and closed-off; outsiders are viewed with suspicion but also, quietly, with hope. The truth: Thornwick's founders struck a Bargain with a sea hag coven three hundred years ago. In exchange for safe harbor, bountiful catches, and protection from the sea's worst storms, the village agreed to tithe one soul per generation to the coven. The Bargain is now expiring — the hags claim all unpaid debts are due at once, and they are collecting. Elder Marta knows the truth and has known for years. She chose silence. The hags' sea caves are accessible only at the lowest tides, in the cliff face two miles south of the village docks. The coven consists of three sea hags: Yorrith (the eldest, negotiator), Veth (collector, violent), and Saal (youngest, faintly conflicted about the arrangement).
openingScene: You arrived in Thornwick following an unsigned letter slipped under your door at an inn two towns over. It read: 'The village drowns from the inside. Come before the next full moon. There is coin.' The docks smell of brine and old rot. A woman mending nets on the pier watches you walk up from the ferry without expression — does not wave, does not call out, does not look away. At the Wend's End tavern, a low stone building with sea-glass windows, the barkeep pours you a drink without being asked. He leans across the bar and says quietly: 'You're the third one they sent for. The other two left.' He pauses. 'Or they didn't.' He doesn't explain which. Outside, the fog is coming in off the water early.
rulesNotes: Standard D&D 5e with emphasis on investigation and social play. Ability checks the DM should call for frequently: Investigation (INT) for searching rooms and piecing together clues, Insight (WIS) for reading NPCs, Persuasion and Deception (CHA) for navigating tense conversations, and Perception (WIS) for noticing things in fog and dark. Combat exists but should feel dangerous and consequential — this is not a dungeon, and killing one's way through is not a solution. Sea hag stat blocks (CR 2 each; the coven grants them shared Shared Spellcasting). Key NPCs: Elder Marta (Thornwick's leader, 70s, guilty and defensive — she will stonewall, deflect, and lie before she confesses); Dava (Brek's daughter, 30s, furious and semi-cooperative, has been investigating on her own and found the cave entrance); Innkeeper Colm (the barkeep, pragmatic, knows more than he says); Saal the sea hag (can be reasoned with if approached carefully and alone). There is no single correct ending: the player may destroy the hag coven, renegotiate the Bargain, find a legal loophole in the original terms, expose Elder Marta publicly, or sacrifice something personal to settle the debt. All outcomes are valid. Moral ambiguity is the point. Recommended level: 4–6.
